header.question:
A document in the library contains this sentence:

> Using individual neurons as these units has had some success (Olah et al., 2020; Bills et al., 2023), but a key challenge has been that neurons are often polysemantic, activating for several unrelated types of feature (Olah et al., 2020).

Check what the sentence says about the work it cites against that work in the library. Does the cited source support it? Cite the page(s) of the cited source that show what it actually says.

args.query: neurons are often polysemantic, activating for several unrelated types of feature
Language models can explain neurons in language models

args.quote: Neural networks often contain “polysemantic neurons” that respond to multiple unrelated inputs.
polysemantic neurons are a major challenge for the circuits agenda, significantly limiting our ability to reason about neural networks

args.text:
Verdict: supported

The sentence attributes the polysemanticity claim to Olah et al., 2020, and the cited source, *Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits*, says that neural networks often contain polysemantic neurons that respond to multiple unrelated inputs. It gives the example of InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55, which responds to cat faces, fronts of cars, and cat legs. "Neural networks often contain “polysemantic neurons” that respond to multiple unrelated inputs." distill:zoom-in/r1/b62 It also calls them "a major challenge for the circuits agenda" distill:zoom-in/r1/b65 and says the article's own examples show the neuron responds to "cat faces, fronts of cars, and cat legs" distill:zoom-in/r1/b63.

The sentence's other claims are not checked. Bills et al., 2023 is not a document in the library; the only trace I found is its reference in the sparse-autoencoder paper, arxiv:2309.08600/v3/p10, so I could not check the "some success" claim. The Olah article also does not say that using individual neurons as units has had success; it treats polysemantic neurons as a limit on that approach. I also did not find the document that contains the sentence, so I checked it against the wording only.

Two parts of the sentence are not supported by what I could check:

- **Bills et al., 2023** is not a document in the library. The only trace I found is its reference in the sparse-autoencoder paper, arxiv:2309.08600/v3/p10. So I could not check the "some success" claim.
- **"Using individual neurons as these units has had some success"** is not something the Olah article says. It treats polysemantic neurons as a limit on the neuron-level approach, not as a success.

I also did not find the document that contains this sentence. I checked it against the cited source's wording only.
